description:
Payloads and results of the built-in v0.1 command kinds (PLAN.md §7.3). A Command carries the
request in CommandBody.payload (google.protobuf.Any); the CommandUpdate carries the serialized
result in `result`. The kind table (lane and flags) lives in @better-compute/protocol
(`commandKinds`) and in the daemon's dispatcher; both must agree.

Stability: FROZEN with agent/v1. Changes are additive only. Later kinds (diag.dcgm, wipe,
deploy.*, boot.kexec, driver.invoke, daemon.upgrade, …) add their own messages.

description:
NodeInventory v1 (PLAN.md §10.1; docs/research/prior-art.md §4).

Stability: FROZEN with agent/v1. Changes are additive only.

Inventory travels as sections (InventorySection in session.proto). Each section message below is
canonicalized before encoding: repeated fields are sorted by their stable key (NUMA and GPU
index, disk name, NIC MAC, peer UUID, link number), and volatile readings (temperatures, power
draw, clocks, utilization) are never part of inventory; they are telemetry (P8). The section hash
is SHA-256 over those exact bytes. No section contains a map, so the encoding is deterministic.

Derived values are not reported here: gpuProduct (normalized NVML name, e.g. "H100-SXM5-80GB"),
gpuModel (family, e.g. "H100", via gpu-models.json), labels and conditions come from the
control plane's inventory module.

messages.name: NodeInventory

An assembled snapshot: what the control plane stores (append-only) and what an inspect driver
returns. Never hashed as a whole.

description:
The daemon ↔ control-plane protocol (PLAN.md §7): join, renew, the bidi Session stream and its
frames, desired state (NodeSpec) and tunnels.

Stability: FROZEN at the end of P0. Changes are additive only (`buf breaking`, FILE). Messages and
fields marked (v0.2)…(v0.5) are part of the frozen shape but unused until that phase.

Transport (§7.1): the daemon dials gw.<region>:443 through an L4 TLS-passthrough load balancer.
Join is server-authenticated TLS pinned to the gateway serving CA; every other RPC is mTLS with
the node certificate. The gateway relays; it holds no CA or signing keys (P14): Join, Renew and
SecretRequest are forwarded to the api's JoinService / secret broker, which verify node proofs
themselves.

Session lifecycle (§7.2):
  1. The first AgentFrame is Hello. The gateway checks the chain, revocation and role, and that
     the certificate SAN equals Hello.node_id, then bumps node_sessions.session_epoch in one tx.
  2. The first ServerFrame is Welcome{epoch}. Then, if applied_generation < generation, a full
     DesiredState, then a replay of the node's non-terminal commands in seq order.
  3. The daemon replays unacked results (Hello.unacked_results) and events above
     Welcome.acked_event_seq; the control plane deduplicates and Acks.

Epoch fencing: routing and liveness writes (dispatch marks, last_seen, disconnect) carry
`AND session_epoch = $myEpoch`, so a zombie gateway's writes fail. Results, events and status are
facts: they are accepted from any epoch, deduplicated by command_id and (node_id, journal_id,
seq), and observed_generation only moves forward (GREATEST).

Errors outside frames use gRPC status codes: UNAUTHENTICATED (bad or revoked certificate),
PERMISSION_DENIED (role or SAN mismatch), RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (handshake token bucket, retry with
jitter), ABORTED (superseded by a newer session of the same node).

services.name: AgentGateway
services.description: The gateway-facing service every bcd mode (node, site, ramdisk) talks to.

rpcs.name: Join
rpcs.description:
Server-authenticated TLS (serving CA pinned). Forwarded to the api JoinService; the gateway
cannot read the sealed token or forge the signed response.

rpcs.name: Renew
rpcs.description: mTLS, at ~60% of the certificate lifetime. Verified by the api JoinService, not the gateway.

rpcs.name: Session
rpcs.description: mTLS. One live session per node; a newer session supersedes an older one (ABORTED).

rpcs.name: Tunnel
rpcs.description: (v0.3) mTLS. Opened by the daemon after it verified an OpenTunnel ticket.

fields.name: sealed_token
fields.description:
UTF-8 compact JWE of the join token ("bcjt_<id>.<secret>") to the pinned JoinService
encryption key. The token is read from BCD_JOIN_TOKEN or stdin only and never stored.

fields.name: csr
fields.description: DER PKCS#10 CSR for a fresh P-256 key (TPM-resident when available).

fields.name: attestor
fields.description:
Attestor that verifies this join: "join-token" (v0.1); "x509pop", "provisioned", "discovery"
(v0.2); "cloud-iid" (v0.3); "tpm" (v0.5). Empty means "join-token".

fields.name: attestation
fields.description: Attestor-specific evidence (v0.2+), e.g. a site agent's SignedDiscoveryAssertion.

fields.name: role
fields.description: The role the agent runs as. The token decides what is allowed; a mismatch is rejected.

messages.name: HardwareClaims
messages.description:
What the daemon reports about its hardware at join. JoinService derives `hardware_key` =
sha256(product_uuid ‖ product_serial ‖ sorted permanent MACs ‖ sorted GPU UUIDs) after dropping
placeholder values, and enforces the token's `expect` binding and reclaim rules.

fields.name: product_uuid
fields.description: /sys/class/dmi/id/product_uuid, lowercase.

fields.name: product_serial
fields.description: /sys/class/dmi/id/product_serial.

fields.name: permanent_macs

fields.description: Permanent MAC addresses of physical NICs, lowercase colon form.

fields.name: bmc_mac
fields.description: BMC MAC when readable in-band.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Serialized JoinResponseBody.

fields.description: Pinned JoinService signing key. Purpose "join-response", parts [body].

fields.description:
DER certificates, leaf first. The leaf has URI SAN spiffe://<td>/site/<site>/node/<node_id>
and a role OID; no tenant.

fields.name: csr_sha256
fields.description: SHA-256 of JoinRequest.csr: the daemon rejects a response that is not for its own CSR.

fields.name: issued_at
fields.description: Server time at issue, for a first clock-offset estimate.

fields.name: deferral
fields.description:
(v0.2) Set when the attestor could not decide yet: node_id and cert_chain are empty, nothing
was issued and no token was spent. The daemon re-sends Join with the SAME csr (csr_sha256 still
binds this response to it): after `pending.retry_after_seconds`, or with its answer to
`challenge` in JoinRequest.attestation.

messages.name: JoinDeferral
messages.description:
A two-round join (§3.3): an operator approval (discovery → joinRequests) or an attestor challenge
(tpm credential activation).

fields.label: repeated

messages.name: Hello
messages.description: The first frame of every session. Kept small for reconnect storms: inventory travels as hashes.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: Must equal the node id in the certificate SAN.

fields.name: journal_id
fields.description:
The journal's id. A change (journal lost: ramdisk reboot, reinstall, corruption) makes the
control plane fail in-flight commands with retry_safe=false ("journal-lost") instead of
replaying them.

fields.name: proto_min
fields.description:
Supported protocol range (PROTOCOL_VERSION in @better-compute/protocol). Below the server's
minimum the session is restricted to daemon.upgrade (Welcome.upgrade_required).

fields.name: last_epoch
fields.description: The last session epoch this daemon saw (0 if none); diagnostics only.

fields.name: applied_generation
fields.description: The newest NodeSpec generation the daemon holds (converged or not).

fields.name: unacked_results
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Terminal results not yet acked; the control plane dedupes by command_id.

fields.name: running_command_ids
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Commands the journal holds as running; the control plane does not re-send them.

fields.name: last_event_seq
fields.description: The highest event seq written in this journal.

fields.name: inventory_hashes
fields.description:
Inventory section name → SHA-256 of its InventorySection.content. The control plane asks for
sections whose hash differs (Welcome.request_sections).

fields.name: applied_spec_hash
fields.description:
DesiredStateBody.spec_hash of the applied generation, echoed so the control plane can detect a
divergent spec and resend a full one.

fields.name: trust_version
fields.description:
TrustBundle.version the daemon holds and verifies with (0: none). The gateway records it
(node_sessions.trust_version) so a command-root switch waits for every connected node (§13).

fields.description:
(v1.0 §13) The approver set the daemon HOLDS: a bundle's version can be taken while its quorum
part is refused (unsigned change, stale epoch), so trust_version alone would read "up to date"
for a node still enforcing the old approvers. approver_set_sha256 is SHA-256 of the held set's
approverSetInput (empty: no approver keys held).

fields.name: protocol_version

Server time (compute_now()). The daemon keeps the offset to its own clock and evaluates

Newer signing trust, if any. Only accepted when signed by the pinned JoinService key and newer
than the bundle the daemon holds.

fields.name: pending_events
fields.description: Unacked events in the journal.

messages.name: Command
messages.description:
A one-shot action. Delivery is at-least-once; the daemon's journal makes it at-most-once in
effect. The control plane stores `body` and `signature` verbatim and resends the same bytes.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Serialized CommandBody.

fields.name: signature
fields.description:
Worker signing key. Purpose "command", parts [body]. Optional in v0.1; required for destructive
kinds from v0.2 and for all kinds from v0.4 (the daemon's own kind table decides, never a flag
an unsigned body could carry).

fields.name: attempt
fields.description: Delivery attempt (1-based). Outside the signature: informational only.

fields.name: batch_approval
fields.description:
(v1.0, §13 quorum) For a body with batch_id: the operators' approval of the batch and this
command's inclusion proof. Outside the worker signature: the approval carries its own.

messages.name: BatchApproval
messages.description:
k-of-n operator approval of a batch of destructive commands (PLAN.md §13). The scope is a Merkle
tree (RFC 6962 style, SHA-256) with one leaf per (subject, kind, payload), leaves ordered by their
hash (bytewise ascending, duplicates removed):
  leaf = H(0x00 ‖ lp(batch_id) ‖ lp(subject) ‖ lp(kind) ‖ lp(payload_sha256)),
  node = H(0x01 ‖ left ‖ right),
with lp(x) = uint32_be(len(x)) ‖ x, and an odd node promoted unchanged to the next level.
The subject is what the command acts on, computed by the executing agent from the signed body:
  - kinds a node runs on itself (disk.wipe, deploy.image, node.reboot, gpu.reset, boot.kexec…):
    the command's node_id;
  - site-relayed BMC kinds (bmc.*): "bmc:" + <the executing site agent's node_id> + "/" +
    BmcOperationRequest.address, the BMC acted on. BMC addresses are site-local (10.0.0.5 exists
    at every site), so the site is part of the subject: an approval for site A never admits a
    command at site B;
  - site.httpProxy: "node:" + its target_node_id (global ids).
payload_sha256 is SHA-256 of the command's payload (CommandBody.payload.value), binding the leaf
to exactly that operation (image, firmware, power action), or EMPTY for "any payload of this kind"
where the payload is built later (approvers see unbound leaves flagged). The executing agent
accepts a proof that walks to the root from either the bound leaf (its payload's digest) or the
unbound one. Daemons run each leaf at most once per batch.
Signing purpose "batch-approval", parts [batch_id, scope_root, uint32_be(scope_size),
int64_be(not_after.seconds) ‖ int32_be(not_after.nanos), trust_domain]. The trust domain (the
deployment's, JoinResponseBody.trust_domain) is supplied by each verifier from its own config, so
an approval for staging never admits a command in production, even with shared approver keys.

fields.name: scope_size
fields.description: Leaves in the tree: what the operators saw and approved ("reimage 412 nodes").

fields.name: not_after
fields.description: Server time after which the approval no longer admits a command.

fields.name: signatures
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Approver key signatures (Signature.kid names an approver key); duplicates count once.

messages.name: BatchProof
messages.description: The path from this command's leaf to BatchApproval.scope_root.

fields.name: index
fields.description: The leaf's index in the sorted leaves.

fields.name: siblings
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Sibling hashes from the leaf level up; a promoted odd node has no sibling at that level.

fields.name: id
fields.description: ULID; the journal's dedupe key.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: Must equal the session's node id; anything else is rejected UNSUPPORTED.

fields.name: seq
fields.description: Per-node monotonic sequence (nodes.next_cmd_seq); resume replays in seq order.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Registered kind, e.g. "diag.nvml". Unknown or role-disallowed kinds → REJECTED/UNSUPPORTED.

fields.name: payload
fields.description: The kind's request message (commands.proto), e.g. bettercompute.agent.v1.DiagNvmlRequest.

fields.name: not_after
fields.description:
Server time after which the command must not start. Checked before accepting (REJECTED/
EXPIRED); the CommandSweeper expires undelivered commands at the same instant.

fields.name: min_generation
fields.description:
The NodeSpec generation the command presupposes. If the daemon's applied generation is lower
it sends SpecRequest and defers; still lower at not_after → REJECTED/STALE_GENERATION. 0 = none.

fields.name: retry_safe
fields.description:
Safe to execute again when the journal shows `accepted` but not `running` after a crash.
Otherwise that case reports FAILED{"interrupted"} for the controller to decide.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.description: UNIQUE(node_id, idempotency_key); workflow steps use "wf:<id>:<stepId>".

fields.name: traceparent
fields.description: W3C trace context, propagated api → worker → gateway → daemon → driver.

fields.name: self_terminating
fields.description:
The side effect ends this daemon process (node.reboot, boot.kexec, daemon.upgrade). The journal
fsyncs running{boot_id} right before it; after restart with another boot_id (or on rejoin
with another role) it completes as SUCCEEDED{rebooted}. Never replayed.

fields.name: attested
fields.description:
The result is a "this node says" statement: CommandUpdate.node_sig is required (v0.2) and the
worker verifies it against node_certs before any state transition.

fields.name: workflow_id
fields.description: (v0.2) The workflow step this command executes; SecretRequest binds secrets to it.

fields.name: batch_id
fields.description:
(v1.0, §13 quorum) The batch this destructive command belongs to. Inside the signed body, so
a compromised gateway can neither add nor strip it; the daemon then requires
Command.batch_approval + batch_proof.

messages.name: CommandUpdate
messages.description:
Progress and outcome of one command. Terminal updates are journaled until acked and replayed in
Hello.unacked_results after a reconnect.

fields.name: state
fields.description: One of ACKED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, REJECTED, CANCELLED.

fields.name: result
fields.description: The kind's serialized result message (commands.proto), when there is one.

fields.name: boot_id
fields.description: The boot the daemon was in when it produced this update.

fields.name: node_sig
fields.description:
Node key, for attested kinds (v0.2). Purpose "command-update", parts
[command_id, uint32_be(state), sha256(result)].

fields.name: reject_reason
fields.description: Set when state is REJECTED.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Set when state is FAILED.

fields.name: rebooted
fields.description: A self-terminating command completed by the reboot/exec it caused.

fields.name: code
fields.description:
Stable lowercase code: "interrupted" (accepted, not retry-safe, daemon restarted),
"invalid-payload", "internal", or a kind- or driver-specific code.

messages.name: Cancel
messages.description:
Stop a command between actions. Never hides a completed side effect: the daemon reports the real
outcome, or CANCELLED if nothing ran.

messages.name: DesiredState
messages.description:
Generation-numbered desired state. Signed like commands; the daemon stores the last full spec,
its hash and signature in the journal and enforces it while offline.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Serialized DesiredStateBody.

fields.name: signature
fields.description:
Worker signing key. Purpose "desired-state", parts [body]. Optional in v0.1; required when the
spec changes `access` (v0.2) and always from v0.4.

fields.name: generation
fields.description: Monotonic. A generation not greater than the applied one is ignored.

fields.name: base_generation
fields.description:
0 for a full spec. For a patch: the generation it applies to; a daemon at any other generation
discards the patch and sends SpecRequest{PATCH_BASE_MISMATCH}.

fields.name: spec_hash
fields.description:
Opaque id of the full spec at `generation` (SHA-256 over the control plane's canonical
encoding). The daemon never recomputes it; it echoes it as applied_spec_hash.

fields.name: patch
fields.description:
Section-level patch: every section that is SET replaces that section wholesale (an empty
section message clears it); unset sections keep their current value.

messages.name: NodeSpec
messages.description:
What the node should look like. The converger runs one idempotent plan(desired, observed) +
apply per section; observed_generation advances only when every section converged or failed
terminally. A section a daemon does not know arrives as an unknown field: the daemon reports
condition "SectionUnsupported" (reason = the field number) and converges the rest.

fields.name: access
fields.description: (v0.3) Empty in v0.1.

fields.name: site
fields.description: (v0.2, site agents only) DRAFT: its content is defined in site/v1, which is not yet frozen.

messages.name: HostSection
messages.description:
Host configuration units (profile hostConfig, v0.2): nvidia-driver, container-toolkit,
mig-layout, fabric-manager, sysctl, … Converged continuously so drift is corrected.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: The config driver id, e.g. "nvidia-driver".

fields.name: config_json
fields.description: Canonical JSON (RFC 8785) validated against the unit's manifest by the control plane.

messages.name: DevicesSection
messages.description:
Device assignments (§3.4 step 9). The daemon rejects overlapping assignments, writes the CDI spec
/etc/cdi/bcd-<allocation_id>.json, an env file and device ownership, then reports a node-signed
AllocationBound; removing an assignment releases it (AllocationReleased). The daemon never drops
an assignment on its own, not even while disconnected (P6).

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description: (v0.3) Set when binding is BINDING_INSTANCE.

fields.name: env
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Extra "KEY=VALUE" lines for the allocation's env file.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Atom id: GPU UUID, "<gpuUuid>/gi<g>/ci<c>" (v0.5), "<gpuUuid>/s<k>" (v0.5), disk WWN, …

fields.name: device_class
fields.description: Device class: "gpu", "gpu.mig", "gpu.slot", "nic.vf", "disk".

messages.name: InstancesSection
messages.description: (v0.3) VPS instances on this host; the daemon converges each toward desired_state.

fields.name: runtime
fields.description: Runtime driver id, e.g. "libvirt-kvm", "cloud-hypervisor".

fields.name: user_data_ref
fields.description: Secret ref of the NoCloud user-data, fetched with SecretRequest{allocation_id}.

fields.name: gpu_device_ids
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: GPU atoms passed through with VFIO (never overcommitted).

fields.name: restore_from
fields.description:
(v0.5, sandboxes) Boot from this snapshot (an instance.snapshot upload) instead of `image`:
disk and, when captured, memory state. The daemon verifies sha256 before restoring and fails
the instance on a runtime or CPU model mismatch.

fields.name: network_policy
fields.description:
(v0.5, sandboxes) What the instance's NICs may reach, enforced by bcd as host nftables rules on
its taps, whatever the runtime. bcd's own tunnel dial from the host always works.

fields.name: identity_rebind_ref
fields.description:
(v0.5, review 13 H2) After a restore, the guest's per-instance identity (SSH host keys, machine
id, workload credentials) must not stay the snapshot's. A secret ref (fetched with
SecretRequest) of the new identity material; bcd delivers it to the running guest (a hotplugged
raw disk read by a vps-installed guest unit) and reports the ref back in
InstanceStatus.identity_rebound_ref once the guest acked it. Changing it asks for a new rebind.

fields.name: ssh_from_host_only
fields.description:
(review 13 L5) Port 22 of the guest is reachable only from the host (bcd's tunnel dial), never
from other guests or the network, whatever network_policy allows.

messages.name: ImageRef
messages.description: A content-addressed image the daemon may fetch and cache.

fields.name: ref
fields.description: Catalog reference, e.g. "ubuntu-24.04-cloud@2026.09".

fields.name: format
fields.description: "raw" or "qcow2".

fields.name: compression
fields.description: "" or "zstd".

fields.name: network
fields.description: Bridge or network name on the host.

fields.name: addresses
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Addresses assigned by IPAM, CIDR form.

messages.name: AccessSection
messages.description: (v0.3) Interactive access material. Empty in v0.1.

fields.name: exec_ticket_jwks_json
fields.description: JWKS (JSON) the daemon verifies exec tickets against (§7.6).

fields.name: ssh_ca_public_keys
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: OpenSSH-format public keys of the compute SSH CA trusted for break-glass certificates.

fields.name: ssh_principals
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Principals such certificates may use.

fields.name: ssh_revoked_serials
fields.label: repeated
fields.description:
(v0.3) Serials of break-glass certificates revoked before they expired. The daemon writes them
into an OpenSSH KRL (RevokedKeys), so a revoked certificate stops working at the next spec.

messages.name: TelemetrySection
messages.description: Where bcd sends its own telemetry (OTLP). Never the session or Postgres (P8).

fields.name: otlp_endpoint
fields.description: Empty disables export.

fields.name: resource_attributes
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Extra "key=value" resource attributes.

fields.name: headers_ref
fields.description: Secret ref of the exporter's auth headers, fetched with SecretRequest.

messages.name: DaemonSection
messages.description: (v0.4) Self-update target; the Rollout controller sets it within the disruption budget.

fields.name: signature
fields.description: Detached release signature over the artifact.

messages.name: SpecRequest
messages.description: Ask for a full DesiredState.

messages.name: StatusReport
messages.description: Convergence state, coalesced latest-wins.

fields.name: observed_generation
fields.description:
Every section converged or failed terminally at this generation. Never regresses on the
control plane (GREATEST).

fields.name: applied_generation
fields.description: The newest generation held (converging or converged).

fields.name: conditions
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: The node's full current condition set as seen by the daemon (health, drift, section errors).

fields.name: instances
fields.label: repeated
fields.description:
(v0.3) What the host runtimes hold: every VM or container they know, managed or not, so the
control plane can move instances by what actually runs and find leaks (an instance no live row
places here). Latest-wins with the rest of the report.

fields.name: instances_complete
fields.description: (v0.3) `instances` is the runtimes' whole inventory: a placed instance missing from it is absent.

fields.name: pressure
fields.description:
(v0.3) Host resource pressure for the Disk/Memory/CpuPressure conditions (§10.1). Absent when
the kernel exposes no PSI.

fields.name: trust_version
fields.description:
TrustBundle.version the daemon holds, as in Hello.trust_version, reported again once it applies
a newer bundle mid-session (Welcome.trust), so the ack does not wait for a reconnect. 0: unchanged.

fields.name: approver_set_epoch
fields.description: The approver set held after that bundle, as in Hello (set whenever trust_version is).

messages.name: HostPressure
messages.description:
Linux pressure stall information (/proc/pressure/*, "some" avg10, percent of wall time) and CPU
steal (percent over the last report interval).

messages.name: InstanceStatus
messages.description: (v0.3) One instance as a host runtime reports it.

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description: The InstanceSpec.instance_id, or the runtime's own name for an object bcd did not create.

fields.name: addresses
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Addresses the guest holds, CIDR form (guest agent or DHCP leases).

fields.name: runtime
fields.description: Runtime driver id, e.g. "libvirt-kvm".

fields.name: identity_rebound_ref
fields.description:
(review 13 H2) The InstanceSpec.identity_rebind_ref the guest acknowledged (its nonce written
back); empty until then. The control plane treats a restored instance as not ready until it
matches the spec's.

fields.name: section
fields.description: NodeSpec section name: "host", "devices", "instances", "access", "telemetry", "daemon", "site".

fields.name: generation
fields.description: The generation this status refers to.

messages.name: Condition
messages.description: A Kubernetes-style condition (PLAN.md §10.1).

fields.name: type
fields.description: e.g. "SectionUnsupported", "DriverMismatch", "Xid79" (v0.2).

fields.name: device_id
fields.description: When set, the condition concerns one device (atom id).

fields.name: age_ms
fields.description:
How long ago the daemon saw the last transition, on its monotonic clock. The control plane
derives `since` from compute_now() (P9: agents report ages, not timestamps).

messages.name: InventorySection
messages.description:
One inventory section, sent when Welcome.request_sections asks for it, when inventory.refresh
runs, or when a re-collection changes its hash.

fields.name: section
fields.description:
Section name (INVENTORY_SECTIONS): "system", "cpu", "memory", "disks", "nics", "gpus", "bmc",
"os". It selects the message type of `content`.

fields.name: sha256
fields.description:
SHA-256 of `content`. The control plane verifies it and compares it with the hash stored
with the last accepted section; it never re-encodes to compare.

fields.name: content
fields.description:
Binary encoding of the canonicalized section message from inventory.proto (e.g. GpusSection):
arrays sorted by their stable key, no volatile values.

fields.name: collected_at
fields.description: Daemon clock, corrected by the Welcome offset; advisory.

fields.name: schema_version
fields.description: NodeInventory schema version of `content` (1).

messages.name: EventBatch
messages.description:
Journaled events, sent in seq order. Results and transitions are never dropped; metric-like
events are dropped oldest-first when the journal is full.

fields.name: journal_id
fields.description: The journal the seqs belong to (Hello.journal_id).

fields.name: seq
fields.description:
Per journal_id, strictly increasing from 1. Cumulatively acked (Ack.event_seq); deduplicated
on (node_id, journal_id, seq).

fields.name: observed_at
fields.description: Daemon clock, corrected by the Welcome offset; advisory.

messages.name: AttestedReport
messages.description: A node-signed statement about allocations (§6 "Attested kinds").

fields.name: body
fields.description: Serialized AttestedReportBody.

fields.name: node_sig
fields.description:
Node key. Purpose "attested-report", parts [body]. Optional in v0.1; required from v0.2, when
workers verify it against node_certs before any state transition.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: The reporting node (must equal the session's node id).

messages.name: AllocationBound
messages.description: The assignment is materialized: CDI spec, env file and device ownership are in place.

fields.name: generation
fields.description: The NodeSpec generation that carried the assignment.

fields.name: cdi_devices
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Fully qualified CDI device names, e.g. "bcd.dev/gpu=GPU-…".

fields.name: cdi_spec_path
fields.description: e.g. "/etc/cdi/bcd-<allocation_id>.json".

messages.name: AllocationReleased
messages.description: The assignment is gone: CDI spec and env file removed, ownership restored.

messages.name: AllocationFailed
messages.description: The daemon refused or failed to materialize an assignment (e.g. overlap with a live one).

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Stable lowercase code, e.g. "overlap", "device-missing", "cdi-write-failed".

messages.name: Ack
messages.description: Cumulative acknowledgement of durably stored events and results.

fields.name: event_seq
fields.description: Every event with seq <= event_seq in journal_id is stored.

fields.name: command_ids
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Terminal CommandUpdates stored; the journal may stop replaying them.

messages.name: SecretRequest
messages.description:
Fetch one secret for current work. Forwarded to the api secret broker, which checks node_sig and
that the ref is bound to the agent's current step or allocation.

fields.name: ref
fields.description: "secret://…", "vault://…", "env://…".

fields.name: epk
fields.description: Fresh ephemeral P-256 public key, uncompressed SEC1 point (65 bytes). Used once.

fields.name: node_sig
fields.description:
Node key. Purpose "secret-request", parts
[request_id, ref, workflow_id, step_id, allocation_id, epk].

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: Correlates the SecretResponse.

fields.name: jwe
fields.description: Compact JWE (ECDH-ES+A256KW / A256GCM) to SecretRequest.epk. Gateways only see ciphertext.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Set instead of jwe on refusal: "not-found", "not-bound", "access-denied", "unavailable".

messages.name: WorkloadTokenRequest
messages.description:
(v0.5) Workload identity (§12.2, §13): a VPS host's IMDS, bound to one instance, asks for that
instance's token. The control plane mints it only for a live instance placed on this node, in a
pool with workload identity on, for a configured audience.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description: Correlates the WorkloadTokenResponse.

fields.name: epk
fields.description:
Fresh ephemeral P-256 public key, uncompressed SEC1 point (65 bytes). Used once: the token is
sealed to it, so a gateway relaying it never holds a usable token.

fields.name: node_sig
fields.description: Node key. Purpose "workload-token", parts [request_id, instance_id, audience, epk].

fields.name: jwe
fields.description: Compact JWE (ECDH-ES+A256KW / A256GCM) of the workload JWT to WorkloadTokenRequest.epk.

fields.name: error
fields.description:
Set instead of jwe on refusal: "not-bound", "disabled", "audience", "rate-limited",
"access-denied", "unavailable".

messages.name: Drain
messages.description:
Reconnect elsewhere (rolling deploys, rebalancing). The daemon closes the session and redials
after the delay, keeping its journal.

fields.name: reconnect_after_ms
fields.description: rand(0, 60 s) by default.

messages.name: RevocationNotice
messages.description:
This agent's certificate was revoked; the gateway closes the session right after sending it.
The daemon stops using the certificate and does not redial with it.

fields.name: serials
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Serial numbers of the revoked certificates.

messages.name: OpenTunnel
messages.description:
Ask the daemon to open a Tunnel stream. The daemon re-verifies the ticket against the
AccessSection JWKS and its jti set before opening it.

fields.name: ticket
fields.description: Exec ticket: ES256 JWT, 60 s, single-use jti, aud "node:<id>", sid, op.

fields.name: channel
fields.description: 0 = stdin/stdout or the byte stream, 1 = stderr.

fields.name: opened
fields.description: The daemon's first frame on the stream.

values.name: BINDING_HOLD
values.description: CDI hold, consumed by an operator-run workload manager on the node (v0.1).

values.name: BINDING_INSTANCE
values.description: Passed to a VPS instance (v0.3).

values.name: BINDING_NODE
values.description: The whole node, for a tenant deploy (v0.5).

values.name: INSTANCE_NETWORK_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: EGRESS: existing specs do not change.

values.name: INSTANCE_NETWORK_POLICY_EGRESS
values.description: Anything the pool's network allows (as before this field).

values.name: INSTANCE_NETWORK_POLICY_PRIVATE
values.description: Only the pool's IPAM subnet and the host.

values.name: INSTANCE_NETWORK_POLICY_NONE
values.description: Only the host: bcd's tunnel dial, DHCP and ARP; nothing else in or out.

values.name: INSTANCE_DESIRED_STATE_PAUSED
values.description:
(v0.5, sandboxes warm pools) Booted, then paused with its memory resident; resuming is
desired RUNNING. A runtime that cannot pause keeps it STOPPED and reports STOPPED.

values.name: SPEC_REQUEST_REASON_PATCH_BASE_MISMATCH
values.description: A patch's base_generation is not the applied generation.

values.name: SPEC_REQUEST_REASON_MIN_GENERATION
values.description: A command's min_generation is above the applied generation.

values.name: SPEC_REQUEST_REASON_NO_SPEC
values.description: The journal holds no usable spec (new journal, corruption, failed signature check).

values.name: INSTANCE_OBSERVED_STATE_PAUSED
values.description: (v0.5) Paused by the runtime (vCPUs stopped, memory resident).

values.name: SECTION_STATE_FAILED
values.description: Failed terminally at this generation (e.g. an overlapping assignment).

description:
Shared types for every better-compute wire contract (PLAN.md §7).

Stability: FROZEN with agent/v1 at the end of P0. Changes are additive only (`buf breaking`, FILE).

Identifiers are plain strings:
  - node ids, command ids, allocation ids and journal ids are server- or daemon-generated ULIDs,
    optionally with a short type prefix; receivers treat them as opaque;
  - `boot_id` is the kernel boot id (/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id), so it changes on every boot;
  - device ids are stable hardware ids: GPU UUIDs ("GPU-…"), MIG atoms "<gpuUuid>/gi<g>/ci<c>",
    disk WWNs, permanent MAC addresses.

Hashes are raw 32-byte SHA-256 digests (`bytes`), never hex strings.

Signatures (see Signature) are ES256 over a domain-separated signing input:

  input = "bettercompute.v1/" ‖ purpose ‖ 0x00 ‖ part_1 ‖ … ‖ part_n
  part  = uint32_be(len(bytes)) ‖ bytes

Each signed field documents its purpose and parts. Signed envelopes (`bytes body` + Signature)
sign the exact body bytes as their single part, so no canonical re-encoding is ever needed: the
verifier checks the bytes it received, then decodes them. Strings are UTF-8, integers are
big-endian of the stated width, a Timestamp is int64_be(seconds) ‖ int32_be(nanos).

messages.name: Signature
messages.description: An ES256 signature (ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256).

fields.name: kid
fields.description:
Identifies the signing key. For node keys: base64url (no padding) of SHA-256 over the key's
SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER. For control-plane keys: the key's certificate subject key id as
published in the trust bundle.

fields.name: sig
fields.description: The raw 64-byte r ‖ s form (IEEE P1363 / JWS), not ASN.1 DER.

fields.name: chain
fields.label: repeated
fields.description:
Optional DER X.509 certificates, leaf first, chaining the key to a trust root the verifier
already holds (worker signing keys chain to a TrustBundle root). Empty when the verifier knows
the key by `kid` (node keys are looked up in node_certs).

messages.name: TrustBundle
messages.description:
The command/spec signing trust the daemon accepts (PLAN.md §13). Delivered inside the signed
JoinResponseBody, and refreshed through Welcome as a SignedTrustBundle. Rotation: new roots are
added first; the old ones are dropped only after every daemon acknowledged the new version.

fields.name: version
fields.description: Monotonic. A daemon ignores a bundle whose version is not greater than the one it holds.

fields.name: command_signing_roots
fields.label: repeated
fields.description:
DER X.509 roots that certify the short-lived (24 h) worker keys signing Command and
DesiredState bodies (v0.2). Empty in v0.1: signatures are optional there.

fields.name: approver_keys
fields.label: repeated
fields.description:
(v1.0, §13 quorum) Operator approval keys (P-256), held off the control plane (laptops, HSMs).
With any set, a destructive command carrying CommandBody.batch_id runs only with a
BatchApproval signed by `approver_threshold` distinct keys of this set.

fields.name: unbatched_destructive_per_hour
fields.description:
With approver keys set: destructive commands WITHOUT a batch_id this daemon runs per rolling
hour (break-glass only; the default and recommended value is 0). A daemon cannot count
fleet-wide, so any unbatched allowance lets a compromised worker touch every node once:
fleet-wide limits come from the approvers (see quorum_tiers), never from this cap.

fields.name: quorum_tiers
fields.label: repeated
fields.description:
Thresholds by batch size, ascending max_scope_size with non-decreasing thresholds: a batch with
scope_size ≤ max_scope_size needs `threshold` distinct approver signatures (the first tier that
covers it); above every tier, approver_threshold. Small batches can then be approved by a
rate-limited auto-approver (one approver key held by a service outside api/worker, which is the
fleet-wide counter), while large ones need k people.

fields.name: approver_set_signatures
fields.label: repeated
fields.description:
(v1.0) The quorum fields (3-6) are signed by the approvers themselves, not only by the join key
the control plane holds: k-of-the-CURRENT-set signatures, purpose "approver-set", parts
[uint64_be(approver_set_epoch), sha256(approver set input), trust_domain] (see protocol's
approverSetInput; the verifier's own trust domain). Published on every version while the set is
current. One rule (review 10 M3): a daemon holding set H at epoch e adopts (set N, epoch e') only
when e' > e AND k-of-H (H's threshold) signatures over (e', N, domain) verify; otherwise it keeps
(H, e). That holds for N == H too: adopting a higher epoch for an unchanged set needs the set's
own signatures. The list therefore carries both the previous set's signatures (which admit the
change) and the new set's own signatures (which move daemons already holding it, or holding it
again after a revert, to the new epoch, so a replay of an intermediate epoch fails). When the
quorum part is refused, the rest of the bundle (roots, version) still applies. A daemon without
keys takes the first set as-is unless pinned (approver_set_sha256 in its config). Residual risk:
a daemon offline across two changes can be served an intermediate epoch by a compromised api;
pin long-offline nodes again when they return.

fields.name: approver_set_epoch
fields.description:
(v1.0) The epoch of the quorum fields (3-6): monotonic, separate from `version` (roots rotate
without touching it), raised with every change of the set.

messages.name: ApproverKey
messages.description: One operator approval key.

fields.name: kid
fields.description: base64url (no padding) SHA-256 of spki_der, as Signature.kid names it.

fields.name: spki_der
fields.description: SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER of the P-256 key.

messages.name: SignedTrustBundle
messages.description:
A TrustBundle signed by the pinned JoinService signing key, so a gateway cannot inject roots.
Signing purpose "trust-bundle", parts [body].

fields.name: body
fields.description: Serialized TrustBundle.

messages.name: DriverManifest
messages.description:
What a daemon-side driver (built into bcd or served over bcx) offers (PLAN.md §5.4, §5.5).
Advertised in Hello.drivers and returned by bcx DriverPlugin.Describe; the control plane merges
it into its registry as a remote driver scoped to the advertising agents.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Driver id, e.g. "redfish", "ipmi", "libvirt-kvm", "nvidia".

fields.name: version
fields.description: Semantic version of the driver implementation.

fields.name: kinds
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Driver kinds it implements, e.g. "power", "management", "runtime", "config".

fields.name: config_schema_json
fields.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 of the driver's config (manifest().jsonSchema() on the TS side).

fields.name: capabilities
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Free-form capability flags, e.g. "virtual-media", "uefi-http".

fields.name: retry_safe_operations
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Operations that are safe to repeat after an interruption, as "<kind>.<operation>".

enums.name: RunsOn
enums.description: Where a step or driver runs (PLAN.md §5.1 `RunsOn`).

enums.name: AgentRole
enums.description:
The role carried by an agent's certificate (role OID) and declared in Hello (PLAN.md §6). Not
the node's scheduling role (`nodes.role`: unassigned, host, dedicated, site).

values.name: AGENT_ROLE_NODE
values.description: `bcd node`: every server; 24 h certificate.

values.name: AGENT_ROLE_SITE
values.description: `bcd site`: DHCP proxy, iPXE, image cache, BMC access (v0.2); 24 h certificate.

values.name: AGENT_ROLE_RAMDISK
values.description: `bcd ramdisk`: PXE commissioning (v0.2); restricted certificate, at most 2 h.

enums.name: Lane
enums.description: Command lanes (PLAN.md §6, §7.5). Each lane has its own daemon worker pool and credit budget.

values.name: LANE_CONTROL
values.description: Short, latency-sensitive work: diagnostics, inventory, reboots, resets. Default credits 8.

values.name: LANE_PROVISION
values.description: Provisioning steps: wipe, deploy, kexec (v0.2). Default credits 4.

values.name: LANE_BULK
values.description: Large transfers and slow jobs: log collection, image pre-warm. Default credits 2.

enums.name: CommandState
enums.description:
The command lifecycle (PLAN.md §7.4). The control plane stores every state; a daemon reports only
ACKED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, REJECTED and CANCELLED in CommandUpdate.

  pending → dispatched(epoch) → acked → running → succeeded | failed | rejected
  pending → expired (CommandSweeper, past not_after);   any non-terminal → cancelled

values.name: COMMAND_STATE_PENDING
values.description: Stored, not yet sent. A BUSY rejection returns a command here with a backoff.

values.name: COMMAND_STATE_DISPATCHED
values.description: Sent on the session with the given epoch.

values.name: COMMAND_STATE_ACKED
values.description: The daemon journaled it as `accepted` (fsynced before any side effect).

values.name: COMMAND_STATE_RUNNING
values.description: The side effect has started.

values.name: COMMAND_STATE_FAILED
values.description: Terminal failure; CommandUpdate.error says why (e.g. "interrupted").

values.name: COMMAND_STATE_REJECTED
values.description: Refused before any side effect; CommandUpdate.reject_reason says why.

values.name: COMMAND_STATE_EXPIRED
values.description: Never delivered before not_after (control plane only).

values.name: COMMAND_STATE_CANCELLED
values.description: Stopped by Cancel between actions. A completed side effect is reported as its real outcome.

enums.name: CommandRejectReason
enums.description: Why a daemon refused a command before any side effect (PLAN.md §6 "Checks before accepting").

values.name: COMMAND_REJECT_REASON_UNSUPPORTED
values.description: Unknown kind, or a kind this agent role may not run.

values.name: COMMAND_REJECT_REASON_BAD_SIGNATURE
values.description: Missing, unknown-kid or invalid signature on a kind that requires one (destructive, v0.2).

values.name: COMMAND_REJECT_REASON_EXPIRED
values.description: Past not_after (server time, via the Welcome offset).

values.name: COMMAND_REJECT_REASON_STALE_GENERATION
values.description: min_generation still not applied at not_after.

values.name: COMMAND_REJECT_REASON_BUSY
values.description:
No free credit on the command's lane. NOT terminal: the control plane puts the command back to
pending with not_before = compute_now() + backoff (1 s → 30 s).

values.name: COMMAND_REJECT_REASON_BATCH_UNAPPROVED
values.description:
(v1.0) A destructive command with a batch_id but no valid BatchApproval covering it (too few
distinct approver signatures, expired, or an inclusion proof that does not reach scope_root).

values.name: COMMAND_REJECT_REASON_UNBATCHED_LIMIT
values.description: (v1.0) Over TrustBundle.unbatched_destructive_per_hour.

description:
bcx: the out-of-process driver protocol (PLAN.md §5.5), served by plugins to both bcd and the
control plane (externalDriver, remoteDriver).

Stability: DRAFT / UNSTABLE until v0.5. Excluded from `buf breaking` (buf.yaml).

Handshake (go-plugin style): the host execs the plugin with a magic cookie and a socket
directory; the plugin prints `bcx|1|unix|<socket>|grpc|<cert>` on stdout; the host dials the
socket with auto-mTLS. Plugins are sha256-pinned and run under their own uid with seccomp and
cgroup limits.

rpcs.name: Validate
rpcs.description: Validate a driver config against the driver's manifest and live checks.

rpcs.name: Invoke
rpcs.description: Run one operation; streams progress, then exactly one result or error.

rpcs.name: Stream
rpcs.description: Duplex byte stream for consoles and similar (first request frame is `open`).

description:
Site agent contracts (`bcd site`, PLAN.md §3.5, §8.5): boot lease state, proxy-DHCP entries,
iPXE scripts, BMC operations and discovery assertions.

Stability: DRAFT / UNSTABLE until v0.2. Excluded from `buf breaking` (buf.yaml); fields and
messages may change without notice. Site agents speak the agent/v1 Session; these messages are
payloads of site command kinds and the `site` section of agent/v1 NodeSpec.

messages.name: SiteSpec
messages.description: The `site` section of a site agent's NodeSpec.

fields.name: cache_images
fields.label: repeated
fields.description:
Images the site cache pre-warms (§11.5), from its pools' policy. The agent pulls each one and
re-verifies its digest before serving it.

fields.name: proxy_targets
fields.label: repeated
fields.description:
The machines site.httpProxy may reach through this agent, each with its addresses: the source of
"an address of target_node_id known to the site" (HttpProxyRequest). The agent refuses a request
whose URL host is not one of target_node_id's addresses (IP literals compared as IPs, names
compared by name and then by every resolved IP), so a request "about" one node can never reach
another machine or a BMC. Contributed for nodes whose profile is agent-less (e.g. Talos).

fields.name: addresses
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: IP literals or DNS names of the node's API endpoint(s), never a BMC address.

messages.name: CacheImage
messages.description: A verified catalog image the site cache holds.

fields.name: sha256
fields.description: SHA-256 of the image bytes.

fields.name: format
fields.description: "qcow2", "raw", "iso", …

messages.name: BootLeaseState
messages.description:
The site:<id>:boot lease as published by the SiteBoot controller. Only the active holder answers
proxyDHCP, serves iPXE scripts and vouches for discovery. An agent that loses its session
self-fences after ttl_ms: it stops all three.

fields.name: epoch
fields.description:
Lease epoch; every assertion the agent signs carries it, and the control plane rejects older
epochs.

messages.name: ProxyDhcpEntry
messages.description: One machine the active boot server answers for (boot.prepareRamdisk / boot.cleanUp).

fields.name: mac
fields.description: PXE MAC, lowercase colon form.

fields.name: boot_file
fields.description: First-stage boot file served over TFTP or HTTP (e.g. an iPXE build).

fields.name: ipxe_script_url
fields.description: HTTPS URL of this machine's iPXE script, served by the site agent.

fields.name: not_after
fields.description: Server time after which the entry is dropped.

fields.name: discovery_token_ref
fields.description:
Secret ref of this machine's MAC-bound discovery join token. The site agent fetches it with
SecretRequest{workflow_id} and puts it only into the ramdisk's boot parameters it serves, so the
token never travels in plaintext in commands.body.

messages.name: HttpProxyRequest
messages.description:
site.httpProxy: one HTTPS request made by the site agent on the control plane's behalf, for
agent-less profiles (e.g. Talos, PLAN.md §5.6 walkthrough 3) whose API is reachable only inside the
site. P5 holds: the control plane never dials into a site. The agent enforces, whatever the command
says: the host resolves to an address of `target_node_id` known to the site (its inventory or BMC
network), https only unless the address is on the provisioning VLAN, no redirects, a response cap
(default 1 MiB) and the timeout. Anything else fails with "forbidden-target".

fields.name: target_node_id
fields.description: The node the request is about; the target host must be one of its addresses.

fields.name: method
fields.description: "GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE".

fields.name: tls_spki_sha256
fields.description: Pinned SubjectPublicKeyInfo SHA-256 of the target's TLS certificate (Talos uses its own CA).

fields.name: secret_headers
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: Headers whose values are secret refs, fetched with SecretRequest and never logged.

fields.name: truncated
fields.description: The body exceeded the cap and was cut.

messages.name: BootCleanUpRequest
messages.description: boot.cleanUp: drops the machine's proxy-DHCP entries and iPXE script (workflow cleanup).

fields.name: macs
fields.label: repeated
fields.description: PXE MACs whose entries to drop; empty drops every entry of the node.

messages.name: IpxeScriptRequest
messages.description:
The parameters iPXE sends when chainloading (${mac}, ${uuid}, ${buildarch}, ${platform}, …).
The site agent matches them against its entries; an unknown machine becomes a discovery event.

fields.name: buildarch
fields.description: iPXE ${buildarch}: "x86_64", "arm64", "i386".

fields.name: platform
fields.description: iPXE ${platform}: "efi", "pcbios".

fields.name: script
fields.description: The rendered script, starting with "#!ipxe". Carries the single-use discovery credential.

messages.name: BmcOperationRequest
messages.description: A BMC operation run by a site agent through bmclib (steps with runsOn: site).

fields.name: driver
fields.description: "redfish" or "ipmi" (or a vendor driver).

fields.name: address
fields.description: Host or URL of the BMC.

fields.name: credentials_ref
fields.description: Secret ref of the BMC credentials, fetched with SecretRequest; never a value.

fields.name: operation
fields.description:
"<kind>.<operation>", e.g. "power.setPower", "management.setBootDevice",
"virtual-media.insert", "inspect.inspect".

fields.name: args_json
fields.description: Operation arguments, canonical JSON.

fields.name: tls_spki_sha256
fields.description: SHA-256 of the BMC certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, when pinned.

fields.name: result_json
fields.description: Operation result, canonical JSON (e.g. {"power":"on"}).
